title: Chapter XIII

teacherSummary.text: Spring comes, and Safie, an Arabian woman beloved by Felix, arrives. As Felix teaches her using Volney's 'Ruins of Empires,' the creature learns language and history alongside her. He learns of wealth, rank and injustice, realizes he has no family, money or name, and asks, 'What was I?' Knowledge deepens his misery.

segments.activity: Model the close reading of the anchor quotation using the written think-aloud below.
segments.script: First, meaning. I read “I heard of the division of property, of immense wealth and squalid poverty; of rank, descent, and noble blood” slowly and put it in my own words: Listening to Felix teach Safie, the creature hears about property, great wealth and terrible poverty, rank and noble blood. Next, craft. I notice the paired opposites, immense wealth against squalid poverty, which show how unequal society is. The strongest word is “squalid”: it means filthy and wretched, a harsh word for the poverty society tolerates. Then, effect. What does the creature learn about human society? My answer: The creature learns that human society values wealth and noble birth, and he has neither; this knowledge makes him feel even more an outcast.
